content: Never chain rebase+merge for multiple agent branches in one command. Do them one at a time: (1) stash dirty state, (2) rebase one branch onto main, (3) ff-only merge, (4) repeat for next branch, (5) stash pop. Also remove worktrees BEFORE attempting rebase — git rebase fails if the branch is checked out in any worktree. The safe sequence is: git worktree remove --force, then git stash, then git rebase main <branch>, then git merge --ff-only <branch>, then git branch -d <branch>.
PreToolUse hooks must use permissionDecision: deny, not decision: block. The latter is silently ignored by Claude Code, meaning guard hooks appear to work in unit tests but don

cd into a worktree directory persists in the Bash tool cwd. If that worktree is then removed, ALL subsequent bash commands fail with exit code 1 and no output. The only fix is /clear to reset the shell session. Prevention: never cd into worktrees — use absolute paths for go test and other commands.
8 parallel subagents can work on the same main branch with git pull --rebase before commit — zero integration issues across 16 beads if agents touch different packages

claude -p hangs silently when spawned as subprocess — 0.79s CPU over 8min, no output, no stderr, no debug output. Process starts and accepts pipes but never produces output. Blocks oro worker bead execution.
claude -p hangs when stdin is a pipe because Ink (Claude Code TUI framework) calls setRawMode on process.stdin which blocks on pipes. Fix: don

cherry-pick works better than rebase for incremental merges when other worktrees exist — rebase guard hook blocks git rebase when any branch is checked out in a worktree, but cherry-pick bypasses this entirely
handleReadyForReview was not passing AcceptanceCriteria or BeadTitle to the ops review agent — the reviewer had zero bead context. Always check what data flows through to spawned subagents.

TestWorkerOversizeMessage flaky root cause: SetReadDeadline(1s) on net.Pipe() serverConn is never cleared after heartbeat read. Expired deadline causes write goroutine
oro work --resume races with worktree cleanup — worker exits, cleanup deletes worktree, then --resume fails because dir is gone. Auto-detect worktree state eliminates the flag entirely.
Running 2 oro workers simultaneously can cause signal:killed — likely resource contention with 2 claude processes. Running 1 at a time is more reliable.
ForPrompt() is already wired in 3 dispatcher call sites (assignBead, fetchBeadMemories, registerWorker) — epic description is stale on this point

CLI defaultMemoryStore() in cmd/oro/store.go:13 opens paths.MemoryDBPath (~/.oro/memories.db) but dispatcher uses paths.StateDBPath (~/.oro/state.db) — workers insert to state.db but oro memories list reads memories.db

Two settings.json files exist — repo-local .claude/settings.json (relative paths, checked into git) and oro-init generated ~/.oro/projects/<name>/settings.json (absolute paths). They drift independently and have different hook sets.
ensureSearchHook in preflight.go fail-opens on build failure but fail-closes on missing srcDir — wiring it into oro start would break go-install users who run from non-repo dirs
no_cd_guard used git rev-parse --show-toplevel which returns worktree root when CWD is inside worktree. Fix: use --git-common-dir which returns shared .git dir, then take parent
quality_gate.sh hardcoded ./node_modules/.bin/ paths fail in worktrees. Fix: resolve REPO_ROOT via git rev-parse --git-common-dir, set NODE_BIN=REPO_ROOT/node_modules/.bin
oro work ff-only merge fails when main moves during ops review. Worker exits code 2. Manual merge needed: remove worktree, rebase onto main, ff-only merge
